items.name: Elara's Doll
items.in_room: At the foot of the largest oak, half pressed into the leaf mould, there is a rag doll with a stitched face.
items.description: Homemade, well-loved, and dry — which it should not be, after three days of rain under an open sky.
items.on_take:
You lift it and the leaf mould comes away in a neat disc, the way turned earth does. The doll is dry. Three days of rain have fallen on this grove and not one of them has touched it.

The scored bark above you is at the height of a grown man's eye. The marks were made from inside the ring, facing out.
items.say_on_take: Dry. After three days of rain, dry. Somebody has been keeping this for her.

items.name: The Bloodstone Geode
items.in_room: The veins converge on a hollow in the rock the size of a cart, and the hollow is not empty.
items.description: A geode taller than a man, its interior crowded with red crystal. The warmth in the workings comes from here. So does the grain in every wall you have passed.
items.on_destroy:
It takes longer than it should, and it does not shatter so much as give up. The red goes out of the crystal from the centre outward, and the warmth goes with it.

Somewhere above, in the palace district, a great many lamps gutter at once and then steady. The veins in the walls around you are grey now, and they are only rock.
items.say_on_destroy: Break it. Whatever the city has been drinking from, it stops now.

items.name: The Undertaker's Ledger
items.in_room: A burial ledger sits among the unclaimed commissions, open at this week's page.
items.description: Four entries this week in a town that usually manages one a month. Against each, in a different hand from the undertaker's, a small mark.
items.on_take: You take the ledger. The four marks are identical, and they are not a religious sign. Whoever made them did it after the entries were written, and did it in a hurry.
items.say_on_take: The Brother buried four this week. This ledger says six.

items.name: A Bundle of Sacking
items.in_room: On the swept millstone lies a bundle of sacking about the size of a sleeping child, tied off with red cord.
items.description: Sacking, red cord, and a shape that is very nearly right.
items.on_take:
It is heavy the wrong way. You cut the cord and river stones spill across the millstone, and among them a strip of red cloth knotted the way the Covenant knots it.

Nobody carried a child down this road. Somebody wanted you to believe they had, and wanted you a long way from the Whisperwood while you believed it.

From back up the causeway, faint across the water, a bell begins to ring.
items.say_on_take: Sacking and a stone. She was never here. None of this was ever for her.

items.name: A Letter Under Black Wax
items.in_room: One of the kneelers left a courier's satchel by the mats. The flap is open, and there is a letter in it under a black wax seal.
items.description: Heavy cream paper. The wax carries the royal cipher.
items.on_take:
It is addressed to the keepers of the vault, and it is short.

'Keep them below as long as they are willing to stay. Hale has done well; see that the girl is kept comfortable, and remind him of her if he wavers. — L.'

The seal on the wall is painted plaster. Close enough to read by, you can see the brush strokes. Above you, the stair you came down is full of small sounds, and all of them are coming this way.
items.say_on_take: Royal wax. Read it. Read it twice.

items.name: A String of Name-Tokens
items.in_room: Where the thralls fell, a length of twine lies in the leaf litter, threaded with small carved tokens.
items.description: Eleven tokens of whittled ash on garden twine, each carved with a name in a careful hand: Tessaly. Orrin. Beck. Hal. The kind a family hangs over its door for luck.
items.on_take: You wind the twine round your hand. Somebody in the valley made these, one for each of them, and somebody else went round and took them all off the doors.
items.say_on_take: Door-tokens. Somebody took these off every house. Let us put them where they belong.

items.name: A Drowning-Stone
items.in_room: One of the stones the drowned came up with has come loose from its rope and lies in the shallows, squared off and far too regular to be anything the mere made.
items.description: A cut block of grey stone the size of a loaf, with an iron ring leaded into the top and a mark chiselled into one face: a tower over three lines of water.
items.on_take: It is heavier than it looks. The mark is old, and somebody has cleaned the moss out of it recently, as if to be sure it could still be read.
items.say_on_take: That mark has been cleaned. Somebody wanted it read.

items.name: The Shift's Tallies
items.in_room: The miners' brass tally-tokens lie where they fell, still on their strings.
items.description: Nine brass tokens stamped with numbers, one for each man who went down on the last shift. The foreman hands them out at the top of the shaft and takes them back at the end, and that is how he knows who is still below.
items.on_take: Nine. You count them twice. It seems important.
items.say_on_take: Nine. Brask will want to count them himself.

items.name: The Gatehouse Door
items.in_room: The gatehouse beside the gates has a door of iron-bound oak, and no handle on the outside.
items.description: Heavy, locked, and newer than the gatehouse. Somebody behind it is being very quiet on purpose.
items.on_destroy: It takes a long time, and nobody inside makes a sound until it gives. Then there are eleven of them in the doorway, blinking: servants' children, a clerk's wife, a boy in a choir tunic, and a girl of about eleven with ink on her fingers, who asks before anything else whether you have come from the library.
items.say_on_destroy: Stand back from the door! We are coming in!

items.name: A Reader's Day-Book
items.in_room: One of the Readers had a day-book in its coat, the pages gone soft with damp.
items.description: An archivist's day-book, kept in a small upright hand until about a year ago, when the entries stop. The last one reads: "Sent below to catalogue the sealed stacks. Hale says a fortnight."
items.on_take: The name inside the cover is Pell Aubery, Under-Archivist. There are four more names on the flyleaf, crossed through one at a time in a different ink.
items.say_on_take: Pell Aubery. He had a name. They all had names.

items.name: The Patrol's Watch-Roll
items.in_room: Among what the maw brought up, a leather roll-case with the palace seal on it, chewed at one end.
items.description: The watch-roll of the Third Palace Patrol: eight names, and a tick beside each for every muster. The last muster, the night of the earthquake, has no ticks at all.
items.on_take: Somebody went down the rift after the quake with seven men behind him and a roll to tick them off by. He did not get to tick them off.
items.say_on_take: Eight names. The King will want every one of them read out.

items.name: A Rubbing of the Newest Name
items.in_room: At the near end of the causeway the newest name is cut in plain letters, clean and deep, with the chisel still beside it. A sheet of paper and a stick of wax lie ready, as if whoever cut it meant for somebody to take a copy.
items.description: A wax rubbing of a single name, cut into the causeway this week in a good clerkly hand: WENNA HALE.
items.on_take: The causeway is where the Quiet Kingdom put the names of those it meant to stop first. The Queen has added one on her way down. It is an eleven-year-old girl's, and she has left the wax out so that somebody would carry the news back up.
items.say_on_take: Wenna Hale. That is the archivist's girl. She put a child's name down here.

items.name: The Charter of the Quiet
items.in_room: On the arm of the empty throne lies a tablet of black stone, written close on both sides, where the King set it down to rise.
items.description: The Quiet Kingdom's last law, in its own script and, below it, in Valorheim's, cut later by another hand: the first thing the kingdom above ever wrote.
items.on_take:
They made the Vessel to end everything, themselves first. At the last they could not bring themselves to wake it, and they sealed it instead, and stopped anyway, one by one, the slow way. The seals only hold against something waking on its own. They do not hold against somebody climbing in.

The Queen has not come down here to wake the Vessel. She has come down to wear it.
items.say_on_take: Read it. All of it. Then read the last part again.

items.name: A Sack of Rusted Nails
items.in_room: Down in the spring channel under the quench trough, a sack of rusted nails has burst open in the water.
items.description: Old nails, hundreds of them, the iron bleeding red into the spring.
items.on_take: You haul it out dripping. The water runs clear behind it almost at once.
items.say_on_take: Somebody's spares for the nail-trees. They went in the spring when the sack split.

items.name: A Watch Horn
items.in_room: Half buried in the leaves beside the path is a brass horn on a frayed green cord.
items.description: A Watch horn, dented, the tower-and-water mark worn almost smooth by a thumb.
items.on_take: You shake the leaves out of it. It still sounds, once, thin and far too loud in the quiet wood.
items.say_on_take: Corporal Penn's. His mother should have this.

items.name: A Crate Stamped TALLOW
items.in_room: Wedged in the reeds at the edge of the causeway is a crate stamped TALLOW in red paint.
items.description: A pedlar's crate, swollen with damp, full of forks.
items.on_take: It comes up out of the mud with a sucking noise and a rattle of cutlery.
items.say_on_take: Forks. He nearly died for forks.

items.name: A Bell-Collar
items.in_room: Caught on a thorn at the treeline, a leather collar with a little copper bell hangs very still.
items.description: An old ewe's collar, the bell green with age.
items.on_take: You work it free of the thorn. The bell does not ring, and then, when you have stopped expecting it, it does.
items.say_on_take: The bell from the Ravencrest fold. Marta will want this.

items.name: A Piece of Seal-Stone
items.in_room: Among the rubble by the mill race lies a broken slab of grey stone, carved with the edge of a seal.
items.description: Seal-stone, heavier than it should be, cold on the warmest day.
items.on_take: It takes two hands to lift. Something in the water below the race stops moving when you do.
items.say_on_take: Seal-stone. Harrow will know what to do with it.

items.name: A Strip of Scored Bark
items.in_room: A strip of bark has come away from the largest oak, the scored marks still clear on it.
items.description: Bark scored from inside the ring, facing out, in a hand that was not looking at what it wrote.
items.on_take: It comes away in one long strip, and the oak does not seem to mind.
items.say_on_take: These marks were made from inside the ring.

items.name: The Mill Bell's Clapper
items.in_room: Hanging from a rotten beam over the race, the old mill bell has lost its rope. Its clapper lies below, green with weed.
items.description: An iron clapper as long as a forearm, weed-grown and cold.
items.on_take: You pull it out of the weed. Up on the beam the bell shifts, and is silent.
items.say_on_take: Nobody will ring this for anyone again.

items.name: A Watch Stores Crate
items.in_room: Half sunk in the reeds is a straw-packed crate stencilled WATCH STORES, its lid still nailed down.
items.description: A crate of frost vials, every one of them unbroken, which is a small miracle.
items.on_take: You lift it out very carefully. Frost blooms on the wood where your hands were.
items.say_on_take: Watch stores, still nailed shut. Rook will be pleased.

items.name: The Mine's Loan Ledger
items.in_room: On a nail by the tally board hangs a loan ledger, its cover stamped with the Crown.
items.description: Forty picks lent, forty picks signed for, and nothing written in the column for their return.
items.on_take: You take it down from the nail. Nobody stops you.
items.say_on_take: Forty picks. Venn will want every one.

items.name: A Bundle of Cut Pages
items.in_room: Tucked behind a shelf in the sealed stacks is a bundle of pages, cut cleanly from their books and tied with red thread.
items.description: Every page shows the same seal, drawn from a different side.
items.on_take: The thread is the Covenant's red. You do not untie it.
items.say_on_take: Every one of these is a seal, drawn from the wrong side.

items.name: A String of Prayer-Beads
items.in_room: On a step of the ossuary stair, a string of wooden prayer-beads lies coiled as if somebody had just put it down.
items.description: Ashkyr's beads, worn smooth by a reader's fingers, every bead a small carved sheaf.
items.on_take: You pick it up, and somewhere below, something that was climbing the stair stops.
items.say_on_take: A reader's beads. Aldus can say the rite over these.

items.name: A Canary Cage
items.in_room: Hung from a pit-prop in the deep workings is a little brass cage. The canary in it is very much alive, and very angry.
items.description: A miner's canary in a brass cage, singing furiously.
items.on_take: You unhook the cage. The canary bites you through the bars.
items.say_on_take: Alive. So, probably, is Pell.

items.name: The Crimson Banner
items.in_room: Above the broken gate, the Covenant's crimson banner still hangs, ragged at the edges.
items.description: Crimson silk, knotted the Covenant's way at every corner.
items.on_take: You cut it down. It falls slowly, like something much heavier than silk.
items.say_on_take: Thorne wants to watch this burn.

items.name: A Jar of Cold Ash
items.in_room: The great brazier at the chamber's heart has gone cold. A clay jar stands beside it, as if somebody had meant to gather the ash and never did.
items.description: Grey ash in a clay jar, finer than any fire should leave.
items.on_take: You fill the jar and stopper it. The chamber is quieter when you have.
items.say_on_take: Whoever this was, they are going home.

items.name: The Warden's Keystone
items.in_room: Among the Archive Warden's broken plates lies a keystone of white marble, still faintly warm.
items.description: A marble keystone carved with the library's mark, warm as a hand.
items.on_take: You lift it from the wreck, and every lamp in the stacks goes out and comes on again.
items.say_on_take: The keystone. Hale wanted this.

items.name: A Lump of Red-Veined Ore
items.in_room: In a cart abandoned in the deep workings, the ore is veined with red that seems to move when you look away.
items.description: Bloodstone ore. The veins are warm, and very slightly wet.
items.on_take: You take a lump. It is warmer than your hand, and stays that way.
items.say_on_take: Harrow wants to know what this does in a fire. So do I.

items.name: An Armoury Tag
items.in_room: On the lip of the Rift, a brass armoury tag hangs from a broken spear-haft driven into the rock.
items.description: A Crown armoury tag, number forty-one, on a cut thong.
items.on_take: You work it free of the haft. The spear stays where it is, driven in to the socket.
items.say_on_take: Number forty-one. Venn will know whose it was.

items.name: The Registry Deed-Box
items.in_room: Under a fallen lintel carved REGISTRY lies an iron-bound deed-box, its lock still shut.
items.description: Every deed in the lower city, dry inside the box.
items.on_take: You drag it out from under the lintel. The street groans, and settles.
items.say_on_take: Every house in the lower city. Hale will want this.

items.name: Ashkyr's Silenced Bell
items.in_room: Stripped of its clapper and wound in black cloth, a small temple bell lies on the altar of the Unmaking.
items.description: A bronze bell cast with Ashkyr's sheaf, wound in black.
items.on_take: You unwind the cloth. The bell has no clapper, and rings anyway, once.
items.say_on_take: Aldus will hang this where it belongs.

items.name: The King's Signet
items.in_room: Among the rubble of the fallen guard post, a gold signet ring glints in the dust.
items.description: The royal signet, heavy, cut with the crowned tower.
items.on_take: You pick it out of the dust. It is warm, as if somebody had only just taken it off.
items.say_on_take: The King's ring. He wants to mean it this time.

items.name: A Name-Stone
items.in_room: One of the causeway's name-stones has worked loose. The name cut in it has been scratched out.
items.description: A grey stone with a scratched-out name, heavy with the weight of not being remembered.
items.on_take: You lift it. For a moment you almost know the name.
items.say_on_take: A king nobody remembers. Aldric wants him back.

items.name: A Courtier's Iron Crown
items.in_room: Fallen beside an empty throne-chair, a plain crown of black iron lies on the flagstones.
items.description: Black iron, stamped inside with the armoury's mark and a date eight hundred years gone.
items.on_take: You lift it. It is very cold, and fits your hand like it wants to fit your head.
items.say_on_take: Armoury work. Venn wants to strike it off the books.

items.name: A Flask of Seal-Water
items.in_room: At the lip of the well, a stone cup still holds a little water, clear as air.
items.description: Water from the Well of Seals, perfectly still even when the flask is shaken.
items.on_take: You fill the flask. The water in it does not slosh.
items.say_on_take: Enough to bless one seal. Maybe two.
